body_markdown:
Innovation leaders partner with startups, universities, and all sorts of technology providers. The logic is obvious: no company can innovate fast enough on its own. Given current geopolitical situations like national protectionism and the AI arms race, there is an uncomfortable question hiding behind every partnership: At what point does collaboration start weakening the very capabilities that make you innovative?


In my new report,[Balance-Ecosystem-Collaboration-With-The-Sovereignty-Of-Innovation](https://forrester-my.sharepoint.com/personal/bschaffrik_forrester_com/Documents/Microsoft%20Copilot%20Chat%20Files/Balance-Ecosystem-Collaboration-With-The-Sovereignty-Of-Innovation.pdf) , I’m exploring why innovation sovereignty has become a strategic imperative and outline practical approaches for balancing resilience, collaboration, talent development, ecosystem design, and IP protection in an AI-driven world. Here are some of the highlights:


- **Think about innovation networks like hosting a dinner party.** Invite interesting guests. Encourage lively discussion. Share ideas freely. Just don’t hand over the keys to the house on the way out. The answer is not isolation. Companies that build walls around themselves rarely win. Innovation thrives on outside perspectives, specialised expertise, and access to global talent. The real challenge is learning where to draw the line.


- **The greatest threat to innovation might come from inside the company, rather than outside.** Companies who are extensively outsourcing critical knowledge creation, or reducing junior roles that traditionally produced the next generation of innovators due to AI advances, create a vicious cycle by themselves. The more they depend on external ecosystems, the greater the risk that key intellectual property and expertise drift beyond their control.


The organisations that will thrive during the next decade will master this balancing act. They will collaborate broadly while identifying the capabilities that must remain under their direct control. They will use AI aggressively while still investing in human expertise. They will embrace open innovation while protecting the intellectual property and talent that define their competitive advantage.
